note_sections.t: Re-evaluation of known prostate cancer to discuss treatment options following recent PSA rise and MRI findings.

The patient is a 72-year-old retired primary school teacher who presents for re-evaluation of his prostate cancer diagnosis. He has a history of benign prostatic hyperplasia and has previously undergone a prostate biopsy which revealed ISUP grade group 2 disease. His PSA levels have fluctuated, with values of 5.8 ng/mL in February 2023, 1.7 ng/mL in February 2024, and a recent rise to 6.9 ng/mL in January 2025. He reports mild lower urinary tract symptoms with an IPSS score of 6/35. Socially, he is married but lives alone, with his niece as his next of kin. He enjoys playing tennis twice a week and consumes approximately 3 units of alcohol per week. He is a non-smoker and has no significant occupational exposures. He is currently not on any regular medications and has no known allergies.

On DRE, the prostate is non-palpable with no nodularity or asymmetry detected, consistent with clinical stage cT1c. General examination reveals a well-nourished male with stable vital signs, including a blood pressure of 101/70 mmHg and a heart rate of 60 bpm. No lymphadenopathy or other abnormalities are noted on systemic review.
